messages:
maya: heads up — seeing a perf regression in canary after landing kernelScheduler v3. p95 latency +4% on chat-api under our standard chat_mix load. nsys trace attached.

chris: which part of the pipeline? decode-only or encode/decode mix? batch distribution?

maya: decode-heavy. median batch_size=3, tail has many batch_size=1/2. Repro locally with stress profile. attaching short nsys capture:

maya: ```
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda —output=canary-kernsched-v3.nsys 
# capture ~30s of traffic hitting chat route
```

perf-bot: Note: canary rollout automatically paused due to latency regression alert (rule: api.p95 > baseline + 3%).

jo: I looked at the nsys timeline — weird kernel switching where fused_flash_attn_v3 fires for a few microsteps then we fall back to flash_attn_prefetch. During those transitions I see a stream of small kv_write kernels: kv_write_sm_coalesce (8-16 us each) that weren't present before.

chris: small writes multiplied by many tiny batches could explain amplification. Do writes happen on hot path or async offload?

maya: they're on the hot path. timeline shows nvtx boundaries: 

maya: ```
[decode step 345] -> fused_flash_attn_v3 (ms)
[decode step 346] -> kv_write_sm_coalesce (us x 12)
[decode step 347] -> flash_attn_prefetch (ms)
[decode step 348] -> kv_write_sm_coalesce (us x 9)
```

maya: NVPROF summary (sample):
maya: ```
Kernel                          Calls   Total GPU Time (ms)
fused_flash_attn_v3             112     420.3
flash_attn_prefetch             94      380.7
kv_write_sm_coalesce            632     12.1
kv_read_sm                      218     3.8
```

ralph: kv_write calls are high-count but small latency each — that pattern is a sign of write amplification when kernelScheduler flips between attn variants mid-sequence. I suspect we aren't coalescing writes across micro-batches because the scheduler switches memory layouts and forces a flush.

chris: can you repro with a deterministic seq_len and force scheduler to prefer fused vs classic? I want to see if the policy transition is the root cause.

maya: yes. repro script: 
maya: ```bash
# force policy selection override in runtime config
REDWOOD_KERNSEL_POLICY=always_fused ./bench_chat --seq 64 --batches 1000 --batch-dist "3,1,1,1"
```

jo: Quick perfetto capture shows bank_conflicts spikes during those kv_write_sm_coalesce kernels. bank_conflict_ratio ~0.6 for SM-5 on the small writes. That will serialise and slow down other warps.

chris: two mitigation ideas: 1) don't switch kernels inside a user request (pin the kernel per-request), or 2) add a micro-batching window for KV writes so small writes coalesce into one bigger write when scheduled within X us.

maya: pin-per-request helped in a quick try — p95 returned to baseline. But that increases cost in some long-tail multi-model routes where switching is beneficial.

ralph: we could add a heuristic: only allow kernel variant switches if expected remaining tokens > threshold (e.g., >32) OR if current batch_size >= 6. That keeps small-tail requests pinned.

chris: also consider deferring KV writes to an async coalesce queue with a tight latency budget (e.g., 200us). If coalesce hits, write once. If not, flush. Lower risk than global pin.

perf-bot: Past incident reference: similar kv-write amplification seen in 2023-09-21 run (ticket #INF-834) — root cause then was aggressive prefetch that changed buffer layout between kernels.

jo: I can run a controlled nvprof with a hooked nvtx timeline showing layout transitions. Will try with and without prefetch flag and with pin-per-request.

chris: thanks. please include per-SM counters (bank_conflicts, shared_loads/stores) and the kernel selection trace. If bank_conflicts drop when coalescing writes, we have a strong signal.

maya: noted. i'll open INF ticket and attach repro + nsys/perfetto. tagging eng-runtime and infra. For immediate canary: rolling back kernelScheduler v3 for chat-api route.

dev-bot: deploy-bot: rolling back canary for service=chat-api, release=kernelScheduler-v2.

maya: thanks. follow-ups: jo/chris — coordinate on perf runs, ralph — help spec heuristic thresholds. I'll paste results into the ticket. :handshake:
